entities.name: Pantoprazole
observations: An 80-mg intravenous dose infused over 15 minutes controlled acid output in all 21 patients with Zollinger–Ellison syndrome within 1 hour; mean onset was 41 minutes.
Intermittent intravenous dosing was 80–120 mg every 8–12 hours; 80 mg every 12 hours maintained control for up to 7 days in 17/21 patients, while 4 required escalation.
At study end, mean acid output was 4.0 mEq/h (range 0–9.7) in the reported follow-up assessment; no serious or unexpected adverse events were observed.

entities.name: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
observations: In a 21-patient human cohort, baseline gastric acid output averaged 40.2 ± 27.9 mEq/h (range 11.2–117.9) before intravenous pantoprazole treatment.
Acid-output reduction was reported within 15 minutes, normalization within 60 minutes, and control lasted a mean of 10.9 hours after infusion in a separate report.

entities.name: PMID:10734021 Pantoprazole ZES
observations: Clinical study of 21 patients with Zollinger–Ellison syndrome evaluating intravenous pantoprazole for gastric acid hypersecretion; all patients achieved control within the first hour, with mean onset of 41 minutes.
